citation: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Legal Counsel. Constitutionality of the National Science Foundation's STEM Programs (slip opinion). 2026-08-12. https://www.justice.gov/olc/media/1457731/dl
title: Constitutionality of the National Science Foundation's STEM Programs (slip opinion)
publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Legal Counsel
summary: An Office of Legal Counsel opinion addressed to NSF's General Counsel. It examines nine NSF STEM programmes set up by statute. It concludes that three cannot be administered and must stop, that two have sex-based preferences that can be cut away, and that four, among them GRFP and Noyce, can continue if run without regard to race or sex. It is an executive-branch legal opinion, not a court ruling.
key_facts: Dated August 12, 2026; addressed to the General Counsel, National Science Foundation; signed by Joshua J. Craddock, Deputy Assistant Attorney General.

Programmes examined: Tribal Colleges and Universities Program; Graduate Research Fellowship Program (42 U.S.C. 1869); Advancing Informal STEM Learning; Robert Noyce Teacher Scholarship Program; Advanced Technological Education; ADVANCE; Improving Undergraduate STEM Education: Hispanic-Serving Institutions; Alliances for Graduate Education and the Professoriate; Louis Stokes Alliances for Minority Participation.
Concludes NSF must cease administering LSAMP and IUSE-HSI and may not continue to fund AGEP.
Concludes GRFP must be administered without regard to an applicant's race or sex, and Noyce by giving information equally to all institutions.
Says NSF may treat amounts earmarked for the three programmes as unencumbered by the suballocation provisions.
Does not mention S-STEM, NRT, CAREER, REU, EPSCoR, HBCU-UP or INCLUDES.
Dated August 12, 2026; addressed to the General Counsel, National Science Foundation.
Tribal Colleges and Universities Program (42 U.S.C. 1862p-13) - concluded constitutional; awards to tribal colleges fall within the Morton v. Mancari exception.
Graduate Research Fellowship Program (42 U.S.C. 1869) - may be administered without regard to race or sex.
Advancing Informal STEM Learning (42 U.S.C. 1862q) - may be administered in a race- and sex-neutral manner.
Robert Noyce Teacher Scholarship Program (42 U.S.C. 1862n-1, 1862n-1a) - may continue with outreach administered neutrally.

Advanced Technological Education (42 U.S.C. 1862i) - a sex-based preference concluded unconstitutional and severable; prioritisation of underrepresented populations must be administered race-neutrally.
ADVANCE (42 U.S.C. 1885a) - sex-based elements concluded unconstitutional and severable; NSF may not give or fund preferences based on sex.
IUSE Hispanic-Serving Institutions (42 U.S.C. 1862o-12) - concluded unconstitutional and inseverable.
Alliances for Graduate Education and the Professoriate (42 U.S.C. 1862s-5(e)) - concluded unconstitutional and inseverable.
Louis Stokes Alliances for Minority Participation (42 U.S.C. 1862p-4) - concluded unconstitutional and inseverable.
The opinion does not mention HBCU programmes or CREST (per the fetch extraction).
States the amounts for the three programmes revert to residual amounts within the $938,250,000 lump-sum appropriation for STEM education.
Cites earlier OLC opinions of December 2, 2025 (Education programmes) and June 22, 2026 (Department of Agriculture preferences for socially disadvantaged groups).
quotes: Certain race- and sex-based programs administered by the National Science Foundation violate the Constitution's equal-protection guarantee.
NSF can—and must—administer the GRFP without regard to an applicant's race or sex under the Constitution.
NSF therefore may not continue to fund the AGEP program.
NSF must therefore cease administering the program.
NSF may therefore treat the amounts earmarked for these programs as wholly unencumbered by the unconstitutional suballocation provisions.
The IUSE-HSI, AGEP, and LSAMP programs are unconstitutional.
NSF may continue administering such programs on terms consistent with this opinion.
